summary: Temporary re-identification proof for regression analysis
description: Issue summary: Request a minimal, verifiable re-identification proof to validate a regression flagged by fraud-detection models. Background: On 2026-03-10 our anomaly detector surfaced a spike in false-negative fraud signals tied to a small subset of customer sessions. The investigation team needs to confirm whether two sampled hashed identifiers correspond to the same internal account to rule out model-label drift before rolling back a recent change. Purpose: provide cryptographically-limited re-identification confirmation (yes/no match) for 2 hashed keys without exposing plaintext customer data. This is strictly timeboxed and must follow data minimization controls.
impact: Investigation is blocked; risk of incorrect rollback affecting ~0.2% of live inference traffic. Without the proof, an emergency rollback may be requested leading to increased latency for Dedicated customers and potential billing reconciliation work.
env_details: Prod inference logs (sharded), us-east serving cluster; affected time window 2026-03-09T23:00 to 2026-03-10T04:00 UTC. Keys in question: hk_3f7a2e and hk_9c1b4d (hashed identifiers).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run the fraud-detector job for the time window. 2) Filter by decision_type=PASS where model_version=v2026-03-08-rollback-candidate. 3) Sample sessions where session_hash in {hk_3f7a2e, hk_9c1b4d}. 4) Attempt local join against customer index (blocked).
logs: Attached excerpts available in secure artifact store: s3://redwood-secure/forensics/INT-709321/samples-2026-03-10.txt (access requires two-person control). Hash prefixes and non-identifying telemetry included; no full PII in artifact.
requested_duration: Timeboxed: 8 hours of access window for two engineers (investigation + verifier), target window 2026-03-13 09:00-17:00 UTC. Access must be logged and KMS-audited.
approval_controls: Require two-person control: one privacy reviewer + one SRE lead. Any re-identification decision must be recorded as binary proof (match / no-match) signed by both approvers. No plaintext data may be exported. All activity logged to audit-log-archive and retained per retention_policy_critical_incidents.
initial_analysis: Hypothesis: a batch-sampling bug caused label inversion on a small cohort; re-identification proof will confirm whether the two hashed keys map to distinct accounts or were duplicate session artifacts. Preliminary trace inspection suggests both hashes appear in near-identical KV-cache keys, raising duplicate-handle suspicion.
requested_outcome: Return a signed statement: 'hk_3f7a2e and hk_9c1b4d refer to the same customer account: YES/NO' plus the minimal supporting artifact (signed assertion and audit log pointer). No additional identifiers.
conditions_and_constraints:
- Read-only view only; no export of raw customer profile.
- Access via ephemeral jump host with session recording.
- All actions must be performed under two-person control and captured in the compliance runbook checklist (Confluence link above).
- If re-identification yields a match, engineering must open a separate ticket for remediation steps before any rollback.
